Actiónes nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, aspi: O Lord, we beseech You, precede our actions with Your favor and accompany them by Your help, so that each prayer and work of ours may always begin with You and, once begun, may be accomplished through You.
Ad Lugdunénse concílium a beáto Gregório: Summoned to the Council of Lyons by blessed Gregory the Tenth and created Cardinal Bishop of Albano, he rendered distinguished service in the weighty affairs of the Council, whereby the dissensions of the schism were composed and the doctrines of the Church vindicated. In the midst of these labours, in the fifty-third year of his age and the year of salvation twelve hundred and seventy-four, he died, to the deep sorrow of all, and was honoured at his funeral by the whole Council, the Roman Pontiff himself being present. Sixtus the Fourth enrolled him, renowned for very many and very great miracles, in the number of the Saints. He wrote much, and in his writings, joining the highest learning with the ardour of piety, he moves the reader while he teaches him: wherefore Sixtus the Fifth deservedly honoured him with the title of the Seraphic Doctor.
Benedíco te, * Pater Dómini mei Jesu Chr: I bless thee,   O Father of my Lord Jesus Christ, for through thy Son the fire was extinguished round about me.
Cantántibus órganis, * Cæcília Dómino de: The musicians played, and Cecilia sang unto the Lord,   saying: Let my heart be undefiled, that I be not ashamed.
Clamor meus, * Dómine, ad te pervéniat:: Let my cry, * O Lord, come unto Thee: turn not away Thy face from me.
Cum autem illud ex Evangélio audísset: N: But when he had heard that saying of the Gospel: Do not possess gold, nor silver, nor money in your purses, nor scrip for your journey, nor two coats, nor shoes, he set it before himself as a rule to be kept. And so, putting off his shoes and content with one tunic, having taken to himself twelve companions, he founded the Order of Friars Minor. Wherefore he came to Rome in the year of salvation twelve hundred and nine, that the rule of his Order might be confirmed by the Apostolic See. The Supreme Pontiff Innocent the Third at first rejected him as he approached; but because afterwards in his sleep he seemed to see the man whom he had repulsed holding up on his shoulders the Lateran basilica as it was falling, he had him sought out and sent for, and, receiving him kindly, confirmed the whole plan of his institute. Francis then, having sent his brethren into all parts of the world to preach the Gospel of Christ, and himself desiring that some occasion of martyrdom might be given him, sailed into Syria; where, being treated most generously by the Sultan, and accomplishing nothing, he returned to Italy.
Cæcília * fámula tua, Dómine, quasi apis: Busy like a bee,   O Lord, did thine handmaiden Cecilia serve thee.
De sub cujus pede * fons vivus emánat: f: From beneath whose foot   a fountain of living waters flowed forth: the stream of the river that maketh glad the city of God.
Deus, qui beáto Petro Apóstolo tuo, coll: O God, who together with the keys of the kingdom of heaven didst bestow on thy blessed Apostle Peter the pontifical power of binding and loosing, grant that by the aid of his intercession, we may be released from the bonds of our sins.

O God, who together with the keys of the kingdom of heaven didst bestow on thy blessed Apostle Peter the pontifical power of binding and loosing, grant that by the aid of his intercession, we may be released from the bonds of our sins.
Who livest and reignest with God the Father, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
℟. Amen.
Deus, qui multitúdinem géntium beáti Pau: O God, Who, through the preaching of the Blessed Apostle Paul, hast caused the light of the Gospel to shine throughout the world, grant, we beseech thee, that we, who do keep his memorial, may continually be helped by his intercession with thee.

O God, Who, through the preaching of the Blessed Apostle Paul, hast caused the light of the Gospel to shine throughout the world, grant, we beseech thee, that we, who do keep his memorial, may continually be helped by his intercession with thee.
Through our Lord Jesus Christ, Thy Son, Who liveth and reigneth with Thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
℟. Amen.
Non meis méritis * ad vos me misit Dómin: Not for my own merits   hath the Lord sent me unto you, that I may share your crowns.
Omnes gentes * per gyrum credidérunt Chr: All the nations   round about believed in Christ the Lord.
Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui vivórum: Almighty and eternal God, who has dominion over both the living and the dead, and has mercy upon all whom You foreknow will be Yours by faith and good works; we humbly beseech You that all for whom we have resolved to make supplication, whether the present world home still holds them in the flesh or the world to come holds them out of the body, may, through the intercession of Your saints, obtain of Your goodness and clemency pardon for all their sins.
Oránte * sancto Cleménte, appáruit ei Ag: While St. Clement prayed,   there appeared unto him the Lamb of God.
Sancta María, succurre míseris, juva pus: Holy Mary, succour the miserable, help the faint-hearted, comfort the sorrowful, pray for the people, plead for the clergy, intercede for all devout women: may all feel thy help who keep thy solemn Commemoration.
Sancte Paule Apóstole, prædicátor veritá: O Holy Apostle Paul,   Preacher of the truth, and Teacher of the Gentiles, pray for us to God Who hath chosen thee.
Sedébit * Dóminus Rex in ætérnum: Dóminu: The Lord is enthroned as King forever; may the Lord bless His people with peace!
Spíritum nobis, Dómine, tuæ caritátis in: Pour forth upon us, O Lord, the spirit of Thy love, that, by Thy loving kindness, Thou mayest make to be of one mind those whom Thou hast satisfied with the Paschal Sacraments.
Thronus ejus * sicut sol in conspéctu me: His throne * shall be as the sun before Me: and as the moon perfect for ever.
Triduánas * a Dómino popósci indúcias, u: I have asked the Lord for three days,   that I may consecrate my house as a Church.
